headline: 6 registered methods can build a regulatory network; they differ in scale (one network for all samples or one per sample) and in their modeling assumptions.
points: LIONESS-PANDA and LIONESS-PUMA give one network per sample; PANDA, OTTER, GIRAFFE and PUMA give one across all samples.
Nothing you said favours one method yet; each option says when to pick it.
Picking an option finds your input files and shows a preview; nothing runs until you approve it.

choices.question: Which workflow should I run?

options.label: PANDA
options.description: One TF-gene network across all your samples · Pick it if you want the standard published method or a base for LIONESS

options.label: LIONESS-PANDA
options.description: One TF-gene network per sample, plus the cohort network · Lets you compare samples, or relate them to outcomes such as survival · Slower: it reruns PANDA once per sample

options.label: OTTER
options.description: The same kind of network as PANDA, from a different algorithm · Pick it if memory or runtime is a concern

options.label: GIRAFFE
options.description: One signed TF-gene network (activating or repressing), plus each TF's activity in each sample · Pick it if TF activity may differ from its mRNA level

options.label: PUMA
options.description: One TF + miRNA network across all your samples · Pick it if the regulators include miRNAs · Also needs miRNA list

options.label: LIONESS-PUMA
options.description: One TF + miRNA network per sample, plus the cohort network · Pick it if the regulators include miRNAs · Also needs miRNA list

choices.ordering: Options that match more of what you asked for, and use only data you mentioned, come first.
